headline: iStock, the stock photo library that says it is 'always AI free', also invites buyers to use AI tools to change the photos they have bought, a Digital Camera World writer has found.
score_reason: Pool 2 kept: a light opinion piece on one person's test of a stock photo site, with no reply from the company.
importance_line: Photographers and photo buyers may expect 'AI free' to cover the whole service, but as quoted iStock's promise is about the pictures in its library, and this is one writer's personal test with no reply from iStock.
summary: Digital Camera World writer Ariane Sherine Juniper writes that iStock, the stock photo library owned by Getty Images, tells customers its library is 'always AI free' and allows no AI-generated images, yet invites buyers to 'customise this image' with AI tools that can remove a background or, for example, turn a plant green or a bath pink. She calls the mix comical and argues that stock libraries are trying to please creators who resent AI while not falling behind rivals that use it; the piece carries no reply from iStock.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched text of an opinion piece, so the account is the writer's own. The quoted promise concerns the library's images, not the editing tools.
